newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Nomura to keep Czech IPB as retail bank-CTK.
newsitem.headline: Nomura to keep Czech IPB as retail bank-CTK.

text.p: Nomura International Plc has no intention of selling the retail banking division of Czech Investicni a Postovni Banka in which it soon will acquire a majority stake, the Czech CTK news agency quoted a senior Nomura official as saying.
"Retail banking is an important and valuable part of IPB, and it would be nonsense to sell it," Randall Dillard, Nomura's managing director for central and eastern Europe, told CTK on Thursday.

Last month Nomura won a Czech government tender for the state's 36 percent stake in IPB, one of the four largest Czech banks, agreeing to pay 5.88 billion crowns ($173 million) and to raise basic capital by a further six billion crowns.

With a five percent share which Nomura already controls through the Czech-registered firm Nutshell, Nomura will have a majority stake in IPB when the equity sale and the basic capital increase have been completed.
Speculation has been ripe among analysts that Nomura was mainly interested in the investment side of IPB's business including the funds managed by the bank's unit PIAS.
Dillard rejected speculation Nomura would sell IPB's retail banking division to another foreign institution.
He said IPB would concentrate on strengthening profitable operations, including an expansion of financial products on the mass market, along with a further geographical expansion.
"IPB will continuously strengthen its capital base and liquidity," Dillard said.
"IPB will invest into new technology and expend the maximim effort on attaining the highest productivity as shown by a reduction of absolute costs," he added.
Neither Dillard nor other Nomura officials were immediately available for further comment.
